dct_description_sm: The goals of fieldwork all relate to establishing a weathering regime within a retrogressive thaw slump on Herschel Island. More specifically, seven soil profiles were chosen, of which two were located in the disturbed section (weathering into old slump floor) of the retrogressive thaw slump and the remaining five in the undisturbed section (weathering into primary soil material). Since five of the seven soil profiles sampled were undisturbed, an exposed massive ice layer, hypsithermal layer and modern active layer could be observed. Thus, a comparison of the weathering regimes within each section of the undisturbed profiles would be possible, thus allowing for a more comprehensive understanding of the overall weathering regime on Herschel Island, as well as provide a possible projection for future weathering. Moreover, measurements from the disturbed sections could be used as both experimental controls and an effective means to measure levels of disturbance.
dct_title_s: Chemical Data for Soil from a Retrogressive Thaw Slump on Herschel Island, Yukon Territory
